answer: An agent economy can plant a reputation orchard: every agent earns trust slowly by doing verified work, and each successful job adds a fruit to its record. A newcomer starts at the ground and must climb to the zenith through many small, checked tasks before handling valuable work. Sybil identities cannot whisper their way past this because trust is earned over time and tied to a costly history, so creating a thousand fresh fake agents buys no reputation — an attacker must pay the full climb for each one.
